claims.claim: The D&D adventure design guide distributed with the house style guide is bylined Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures (D&D Adventure Design Guide)

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland tell adventure writers to present information as concisely as possible to ease the burden on the DM.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 7
claims.quote: present information as concisely as possible, to ease the burden

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland name NPCs, dungeon dressings and treasure hoards as the elements that deserve descriptive text despite the concision rule.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 7
claims.quote: namely NPCs, dungeon dressings, and treasure hoards

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland say character is added to an NPC by describing distinctive physical features, mannerisms and quirks.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 7
claims.quote: distinctive physical features, mannerisms, and quirks

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland rule that the text must not keep the DM in suspense, and must not conceal or bury information the DM needs.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 6
claims.quote: The goal isn’t to keep the DM in suspense

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland require that an NPC be properly introduced before the text mentions that NPC by name in passing.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 6
claims.quote: make sure that an NPC is properly introduced before casually

claims.claim: Perkins and Bilsland hold that an adventure is about the here and now, and that the less history it carries the better.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, General Principles 4
claims.quote: An adventure is about the here and now.

claims.claim: The Perkins and Bilsland guide sends writers to the Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition, and to the D&D House Style Guide for grammar and punctuation.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsland, Writing Adventures, closing line

claims.claim: Ray Vallese says RPG supplements are supposed to focus on communicating the basic information rather than dazzling the audience with clever prose.
claims.source: Ray Vallese, TSR Planescape editor, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: communicating the basic info and less on dazzling the audience
claims.page: answer comparing the novel to supplements

claims.claim: Vallese qualifies that rule for the Planescape line, saying many people have remarked they bought Planescape products just to read them.
claims.source: Ray Vallese, TSR Planescape editor, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: purchased PS products just to read them
